question: Why do nurses stand with their feet wide apart when getting ready to lift a heavy load?

options.A: To speed up the transfer procedure
options.B: To increase upper body muscular strength
options.C: To reduce the patient's anxiety level
options.D: To improve overall body balance and stability

explanation: Spreading your feet gives you a solid base. It lowers your center of gravity so you won't wobble, keeping both you and your patient safe from falls! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why must you avoid twisting your waist while lifting a patient?

options.A: Twisting causes the patient to slip out of the nurse's arms
options.B: Twisting places excessive rotational stress on the lumbar spine
options.C: Twisting interferes with clear communication during the transfer
options.D: Twisting increases the physical weight of the patient

explanation: Twisting while carrying weight puts heavy strain on your lower back. Always pivot with your feet instead of turning at the waist to protect your spine! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the most important thing to check before moving a patient?

options.A: The time of day the transfer is scheduled
options.B: The patient's weight-bearing ability and strength
options.D: The brand name of the hospital bed

explanation: Always figure out how much weight the patient can support on their own first. This tells you if they can walk with you or if you need extra hands or equipment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: How should you move a patient who is very confused and cannot support any weight on their legs?

options.A: Assisted pivot transfer using a gait belt
options.C: Total mechanical lift with maximum assistance
options.D: Unassisted walking to the nearby chair

explanation: If a patient can't stand or follow directions well, don't risk a manual lift. Use a mechanical lift to keep everyone safe and injury-free. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: What safety check must you always do right before moving a bedridden patient?

options.A: Placing the bed in the highest position possible
options.B: Removing all pillows from the surrounding area
options.C: Locking the wheels of both the bed and the chair
options.D: Lowering all side rails on both sides of the bed

explanation: Always lock the wheels! Unlocked furniture can slide apart mid-move, leaving a dangerous gap where a patient can easily take a hard fall. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do nurses count out loud together (like '1, 2, 3, lift') before moving a patient?

options.A: It fulfills mandatory hospital legal documentation rules
options.B: It allows the physician to monitor the transfer progress
options.C: It ensures all caregivers exert force simultaneously and smoothly
options.D: It distracts the patient from feeling pain during the move

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Counting together ensures everyone lifts at the exact same second so the weight is shared evenly. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why should you have a patient sit on the edge of the bed for a moment before standing them up?

options.A: To allow the nurse time to chart the vital signs
options.B: To let the bed mattress regain its original shape
options.C: To prevent dizziness caused by orthostatic hypotension
options.D: To encourage the patient to dress independently

explanation: Sitting and dangling their legs gives their blood pressure time to adjust after lying down, stopping sudden dizzy spells or fainting. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: During a standing pivot transfer, where should you place your knees to support the patient?

options.A: Pressed tightly against the back of the chair
options.B: Blocking the patient's knees to prevent buckling
options.C: Resting several inches behind the patient's knees
options.D: Spread wide apart outside the wheelchair wheels

explanation: Bracing your knees against theirs gives their legs extra support right when they stand up, keeping their knees from buckling under them. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h4)

question: When is it an absolute must to use a mechanical lift for a patient transfer?

options.A: When the patient weighs more than fifty kilograms
options.B: When the patient requests to sit in a reclining chair
options.C: When only one nurse is available on the shift
options.D: When the patient is totally dependent and non-weight-bearing

explanation: Never try to dead-lift a patient who cannot bear weight. Using a mechanical lift saves your back from career-ending injuries! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of a slide board during a patient transfer?

options.A: To provide back support for patients sitting upright
options.B: To convert a standard hospital bed into a reclining chair
options.C: To bridge the gap for horizontal transfers between flat surfaces
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the patient in bed

explanation: A slide board acts like a smooth little bridge between the bed and a stretcher, helping you glide the patient across without friction. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to write in your notes after transferring a patient?

options.A: How the patient tolerated the transfer procedure
options.B: The level of assistance required by the patient
options.C: The specific brand name of the mechanical lift used
options.D: Any complications such as dizziness or pain experienced

explanation: You should document how much help the patient needed and how they felt, but nobody needs to know the exact manufacturing brand of the lift! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why is it so important to leave the hospital bed in its lowest position after you finish transferring a patient?

options.A: It complies with energy conservation guidelines for the ward
options.B: It minimizes injury severity if the patient attempts to get up and falls
options.C: It prevents the mechanical lift from getting stuck underneath
options.D: It makes it easier for the nursing staff to perform bed baths

explanation: If a restless patient tries to climb out of bed later and falls, a low bed means a shorter drop and much less chance of a severe injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h6)
